# Endurance audit, replayed with the team's second stop as the horizon

Of 923 published endurance decisions, 844 have a later stop by the same car, and 784 of those can be replayed with the horizon at that stop: the real first stop has to be a feasible candidate once the second stint must also fit in one tank. ## Is the agreement more than the window allows?

In endurance the fuel clock bounds the first stop from above and, once the second stop is fixed, the second stint bounds it from below. The window can be narrow enough to make agreement automatic, so each class is compared against two chance baselines on the same windows: a lap drawn uniformly from the window, and its midpoint. A class where the engine does no better than chance carries no evidence either way.
